Three of its seven axes are already emitted for targets as standalone gates — `check-action-pins.mjs.ejs` and `check-workflow-sha-pinning.mjs.ejs` (unpinned actions) and `check-workflow-perms.mjs.ejs` (missing top-level permissions). The remaining four (concurrency, timeout-minutes, cancellable deploy/audit, branch write-back) have no target twin; closing that is a target D-ACTIONS design, tracked as a follow-up rather than half-shipped here.

INV-120: the workflow job-`needs:` critical-path depth must not regress. Self-only in its PRESENT construction: the thresholds are calibrated against arbiter's OWN rendered corpus — FILE_OVERRIDES pins `01-pr-fast: 3` with an in-script design note explaining that the spec's ≤2 "would fail on the current templates" because of the Java Maven classify-changes → build-reactor → gate → unit-tests path. Those numbers are a property of one rendering: `src/templates/github/workflows/01-pr-fast.yml.ejs` is 1095 lines carrying 208 EJS conditionals, of which arbiter's own 629-line 01-pr-fast.yml is a single configuration, so arbiter's green run proves nothing about a target's graph. A twin therefore needs per-archetype limits derived from the rendered graph rather than arbiter's constants — a design task tracked as a follow-up, not a copied .ejs.
